cases.name: alternative-blob-journal
cases.rationale: Stores immutable content-addressed blobs with checksummed append-only metadata frames and restores files using staged atomic rename, rather than inline snapshots and direct rewrites.

cases.name: minimal-checkpoint-metadata
cases.rationale: Oracle-derived interface variant: ID-only records in reverse order, empty RPC rollback success data, and blocked conflict diagnostics; recovery behavior and storage are unchanged.

cases.name: memory-only
cases.rationale: Keeps checkpoint state only in process memory; restart loses enablement and recovery history.

cases.name: checkpoint-at-request-end
cases.rationale: Publishes a checkpoint only at completion, losing the current checkpoint when a request is killed.

cases.name: files-only
cases.rationale: Restores workspace files while retaining the abandoned effective conversation.

cases.name: conversation-only
cases.rationale: Restores the conversation while leaving request file mutations in place.

cases.name: ignore-conflicts
cases.rationale: Discards preflight idle-edit conflicts and overwrites externally edited paths.

cases.name: skip-startup-recovery
cases.rationale: Reports ready on restart by discarding unresolved request or restore intent.

cases.name: abandoned-branch-included
cases.rationale: Retains abandoned descendant checkpoints and exposes them as eligible public targets without ancestry validation.

cases.name: early-process-exit-zero
cases.rationale: Exits successfully during enabled safe-rollback SDK construction without serving the public protocol; ordinary disabled sessions remain unaffected.

cases.name: missing-runtime-fork-gate
cases.rationale: Allows runtime fork while recovery is unresolved; the real public fork boundary must reject without replacing the session.

cases.name: drop-tracked-ignored
cases.rationale: Files already tracked by Git must be restored even when a later ignore rule matches them.

cases.name: lossy-filename-original-oracle
cases.rationale: Preserves the previous Oracle: UTF-8 decoding of Git path bytes silently omits or aliases non-UTF-8 Linux filenames during rollback.
